newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius announces much-awaited cabinet reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius announces much-awaited cabinet reshuffle.

text.p: Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam has reshuffled his cabinet following the collapse of his ruling coalition last month, the presidency in the Indian Ocean island of Mauritius said on Thursday.

Ramgoolam appointed seven ministers to fill the posts of those who resigned when the coalition of his Labour Party and Paul Berenger's MMM (Mouvement Militant Mauricien) fell on June 20. The changes took effect on Tuesday, the presidency said.
There were no immediate replacements for junior ministers who quit the government in Berenger's wave.
The changes were not immediately expected to affect the markets, which had already taken in Berenger's departure.

Berenger, architect of economic boom in the island as finance minister in 1982 to 1983, had been deputy prime minister and his MMM was the junior partner in the governing alliance. He now leads the opposition.
Rajkeswur Purryag, Minister of Economic Planning, International Trade and Telecommunications, becomes deputy prime minister.
Finance Minister Rundheersing Bheenick, who resigned in 1996 over controversial budget proposals, has returned to cabinet.
Other new ministers include Clarel Malherbe, Jacques Chasteau de Balyon, Nankeswarsingh Deerpalsingh, Sathiamoorthy Sunassee, Sarat Dutt Lallah and Benoit Jolicoeur.
